why: Coverage ratchets upward. These are the values measured when the gate was written,
not targets. --gate fails if any subject drops below its floor, so authoring can only
add. Raise a floor when new teaching lands; never lower one to make a run green.
If a term reads as untaught because the lesson uses a different name for the same idea,
add an alias in the subject's .terms.json — that is the fix, not a lower floor.
matching: Phrase-contiguous and whole-word. Three measurement bugs were found and fixed while
this baseline was being taken, each of which inflated coverage:
1. substring matching put RICE inside 'price', SAM inside 'same', SOM inside 'some';
2. scattered-token matching let the alias 'reach impact confidence effort' match four
unrelated sentences, so the bank's largest untaught idea read as taught;
3. dropping interior function words turned 'Jobs to Be Done' into 'jobs done',
reporting a lesson TITLE as untaught.
Reported coverage moved 63% -> 61% -> 36% -> 39% across those fixes. The floors below
are the post-fix numbers, verified against ten hand-checked controls.
raised: 2026-08-17: SPMS 36 -> 39 after RICE, traceability and the vanity/actionable metric contrast
were authored into SPMS-M07-L01, SPMS-M06-L08 and SPMS-M08-L03 (fix A3). This is what raising
a floor is for: the number moved because teaching landed, not because matching got looser.
2026-08-17: SPMS 39 -> 50 (fix C2a). Module 1 went 3/17 -> 17/17 with six new lessons —
SPMS-M01-L01 to L04, L06 to L08 — covering the four elements of a product, physical versus
software, the four kinds of software product, family/platform/line, the SPM definition and its
eras, startup discovery and validation, and product thinking. Authored from the course's own
module 1 notes, which are handwritten and were read visually rather than OCR'd.
raised2: 2026-08-17: BRGSA 78 -> 100. No new lessons were needed. All 15 remaining terms were ideas the
50 existing lessons already taught under different names, so the fix was to make the prose use
the course's own labels — golden rule, master loop, growth operating system, scaling threshold,
revenue architecture, traction levers, cohort retention table, voluntary versus involuntary
churn, brand snapshot, low-resource validation, A/B testing, statistical significance — plus
four aliases where the difference was pure phrasing. That a well-authored subject could sit at
78% purely on vocabulary is the finding: the gate measures whether a learner meets the words
the exam will use, and BRGSA was teaching the ideas in its own words instead of the course's.
raised3: 2026-08-17: SPMS 50 -> 63. Modules 2 and 3 taken to 100% with eight new lessons —
SPMS-M02-L01/L02/L03/L07/L08 (value pyramid, value proposition canvas, what a market is,
MVPs and learning loops, the two fits) and SPMS-M03-L01/L03/L08 (product vs company vision,

raised4: 2026-08-17: SPMS 63 -> 100. Modules 4-8 completed with 13 further lessons: the pricing
pyramid, the Spotify tiering rule, revenue models and funding stages, business ecosystems,
blue ocean and value innovation, launches and CX, product planning approaches, the requirement

Agile, metric frameworks, and responsible product management. All four SPMS lessons that

raised5: 2026-08-17: SCLM 32 -> 100. Twelve new lessons authored from the course's handwritten
module 1-2 notebook (read visually) plus the revision sheets: what a supply chain is and its
three flows, supply chain surplus, decision phases and the cycle/push-pull views, efficient vs
responsive chains, ROA/C2C/Little's Law, forecast composition, methods and error metrics,
inventory functions and ABC, total cost of ownership and aggregation, risk-sharing contracts,
logistics horizons, rail innovations and systemic bottlenecks, modes and national reforms,
and postponement/kitting/cross-docking. A learner is now told what a supply chain is before

raised6: 2026-08-17: IBM 19 -> 100, and all four subjects now sit at 100%.
IBM needed almost no new lessons. Its 24 lessons already covered the module content; what they
lacked was the course's own labels for it, which is exactly what this gate measures. 72 glossary
entries were authored onto the 20 lessons that own those ideas — the glossary field is defined as
'every term the lecture introduces', so that is where they belong rather than a workaround —
plus three aliases where the lesson uses the course's other name (share value, replication).
Final: 360 of 360 named ideas taught. 42 new lessons authored this session across SPMS and SCLM,
and ~90 vocabulary fixes across BRGSA and IBM. Floors are now all 100, so any subject that drops
below full coverage fails the gate.
